claims.text: Machine-learning models using Holder means of elemental properties and structural properties should be applied to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The material begins as a solid multicomponent high-entropy alloy.
The proposed approach is intended to operate at high temperatures and across various compositions.
Group number, atomic radius, electronegativity, cohesive energy, and density can serve as elemental or structural descriptors for an HEA machine-learning model.
A machine-learning model can determine high-temperature thermodynamic properties by capturing complex relationships among the listed elemental and structural descriptors.
The intervention will improve the accuracy of transition-temperature determination.
The intervention will improve the accuracy of fusion-enthalpy determination.
The intervention will improve the accuracy of fusion-entropy determination.
The intervention will improve the accuracy of volume-change determination at the transition.
The intervention will improve the accuracy of dense-fluid heat-capacity determination.
Accuracy will improve relative to experimental methods, DFT, and CALPHAD baselines.
The approach is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys across various compositions and temperatures.
Model accuracy may depend on the quality and domain relevance of the training data.
Model accuracy may depend on the particular alloy system, including effects such as lattice distortion in disordered HEAs.
Comparison with experimental measurements of the five target properties can test the hypothesis.
A significant deviation between model predictions and experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
